name: RobStride 02
_comment_source: All figures from the RobStride RS02 User Manual (rev 260713), sections 1.2-1.4 and 2.1. Phase resistance, inductance, rotor inertia and the thermal network are NOT published and are estimated by the tool - see the ASSUMED PARAMETERS section of any report.

datasheet.title: RobStride RS02 User Manual
datasheet._note: revision is the vendor's filename stamp; version/date are from the manual's own section 7 Version History. The vendor's version field is inert: the 260713 revision STILL declares v1.0 dated 2025-11-25, seven months and several real spec changes after the 251210 revision did. The sha256 is the only reliable identity - verify with 'eval_actuator.py --check-datasheets'.

gear_eff.note: back-solving vendor Kt_out=1.22 against Ke=9.6 gives 0.99, which is not credible for a 7.75:1 planetary. Both Kt and Ke are quoted to 2 s.f., so the back-solve is degenerate here; class default retained instead. See notes.

Ke_Vrms_per_kRPM.note: manual 1.3.10 quotes this as '0.096 Vrms/rpm', i.e. 9.6 Vrms/kRPM, line-to-line RMS per 1000 rotor rpm

kt_sat_derate.note: 17 N.m actual peak vs 19.8 N.m linear extrapolation of Kt at 23 Apk

tau_cont_out_spec.note: manual 1.2.3 'rated load (CW)'; ambient and mounting unspecified

T_winding_max.note: 260713 revision states 145 degC (actual insulation limit 180 degC). The 251210 revision had this and the RS01 the other way round; the newer revision is taken as the corrected one - a value that swaps between revisions is most likely an erratum that was caught and fixed.

notes: Vendor rated torque of 6 N.m is quoted with no stated ambient temperature or mounting condition, so it cannot be taken as a continuous rating in an enclosed robot arm. This tool computes the continuous limit from the thermal model instead.

The RS01 and RS02 are the same motor with different bus ratings: identical mass, dimensions, gear ratio, Ke, currents and torques. The RS02 is rated 48 V and reaches 410 rpm no-load vs the RS01's 315 rpm at 36 V - the ratio matches the voltage ratio almost exactly.

gear_eff is a class default, not a back-solve. Kt_out (1.22) and Ke (9.6) are each given to 2 s.f., and back-solving one against the other implies 99% efficiency - inside the rounding band but not physically credible. Treat torque-per-amp predictions as +/-6%.
Datasheet no-load speed of 410 rpm at 48 V corresponds to 3178 rotor rpm, about 90% of the line-to-line RMS the bus can supply - consistent with the quoted Ke.
Dual 14-bit magnetic encoders, 1 Mbps CAN, FOC drive integrated. Class B insulation, -20 to 50 degC ambient, no-load current 0.5 Arms.
Housing is 63 mm dia x 28 mm per the 1.1 outline drawing. The 'Dimensions: 58mm' in the 2.1 driver table refers to the control board, not the actuator.

260713 revision adds the rated-load test setup: aluminium-alloy heat sink, 260 x 280 mm, rated load measured at 100 rpm output. The earlier 251210 revision left mounting entirely unqualified. A heat sink that size is a bench fixture, not a robot joint, so the vendor rated torque still should not be read as a continuous rating in an enclosed arm.

Vendor overload endurance (ROTATING and STALLED) is now carried as structured data in overload_curves below. NOTE the rotating table is byte-identical to the RS01's and is treated as a shared observation, not an independent one.

Stall is the case to watch for holding-torque duty: the manual states single-phase heating under stall is 1.414x that when rotating, because the three phases heat unevenly with the rotor stationary. The two-node thermal model assumes even heating and so reads optimistic against the stall table by construction - the report says so.
These endurance figures superseded the 251210 numbers, which differed materially (RS00 at 14 N.m: 5 s then, 3 s now). Any thermal-model fit should use the 260713 values.

tn_curve.note: Digitised from the 260713 manual's T-N curve image (section 1.3, 48 V), read at gridline crossings; +/-1 minor division, so roughly +/-5% in torque and +/-10 rpm. Axes are labelled in this revision, unlike 251210. The RS01 manual prints this same image, but the 200-410 rpm span matches the RS02's 410 rpm no-load rather than the RS01's 315 rpm, so the curve belongs to this part and the RS01 copy is the mislabelled one. Note the RS02 looks like the later higher-voltage derivative of the RS01, so treat its other spec-table values as possibly inherited rather than independently measured.

overload_curves.note: 260713 manual overload endurance, rotating. CAUTION: byte-identical to the RS01's table despite the RS01 being a 36 V part and this a 48 V part. The two manuals demonstrably share content. Treated as one observation shared with the RS01, not an independent one; tol widened to 0.20. Which of the two it was actually measured on is unknown - the RS02 is the later derivative, so if anything this table is more likely to be the RS01's, the reverse of the T-N curve situation.

260713 manual overload endurance, stalled. Differs from the RS01's stall table, so this appears to be genuinely the RS02's own measurement. Single-phase heating under stall is 1.414x rotating; the two-node model assumes even three-phase heating and will read optimistic here by construction.
